identity.title: Licensee Event Report No. 2020-003-00 Cooper Nuclear Station, Docket No. 50-298, DPR-46

cause.proximate_text: The direct cause of this event was at least one bolt on number one governor valve actuator inspection port cover plate was bottomed-out. This was due to on-site vendor craftsmanship being unsatisfactory in the failure to recognize bottomed-out bolt upon actuator installation. In addition, the inspection port cover plate holes on the new number one governor valve actuator body were not threaded deep enough to meet vendor specifications.
cause.theme: vendor installation craftsmanship / manufacturing defect on actuator cover bolting

nodes.display_name: Main Stop Valve and Governor Valve Assemblies
Actuator body holes not threaded deep enough for specified bolt length
nodes.description: Measurements confirmed the bolt could not have been correctly installed because the holes in the actuator body were not threaded deep enough to accept the length of specified bolt.
One bolt on the number one governor valve actuator inspection port cover plate was bottomed-out and prevented appropriate tightening for an adequate seal; not noticed during installation.

nodes.display_name: O-ring ruptured due to inadequate seal
nodes.description: The o-ring was ruptured, resulting in the oil leak.

nodes.display_name: DEH oil leak from governor valve actuator cover
nodes.description: An oil leak was discovered on the number one governor valve actuator inspection port cover plate three days after CNS reached 100% power.

nodes.display_name: Abnormal/low DEH fluid reservoir level and pressure
nodes.description: Control Room received an alarm for abnormal turbine DEH fluid reservoir level, and insufficient DEH system pressure prevented operation of the main turbine bypass valves.

nodes.display_name: Rapid power reduction and manual reactor scram; Group 2 isolation

properties.note: Manual reactor scram removed main turbine from service; power restored to 100% on Nov 4, 2020 at 1153.

nodes.display_name: Appropriately classify critical Turbine Generator Fluid connections requiring additional bolting/torqueing verification
Review final vendor evaluation of actuator manufacturing defects/field craftsmanship and determine if additional actions warranted
Cut bolts short to achieve adequate tightening while maintaining thread engagement

nodes.title: Manual Reactor Scram for DEH Fluid Leak
Manual Scram on Low Water Level Caused by Turbine Trip from Hydraulic Fluid Leak

chain: actuator body under-threaded bolt holes [cause TBD] -> bolt bottomed-out, inadequate cover tightening -> O-ring ruptured -> DEH oil leak from governor valve actuator cover -> abnormal/low DEH fluid reservoir level & pressure -> manual reactor scram, rapid power reduction, Group 2 isolation
notes: Cause code left TBD/provisional per FORM-366 (official code not provided). Narrative describes both a craftsmanship failure (missed bottomed-out bolt during installation) and an underlying manufacturing/machining defect (holes not threaded deep enough) as contributing direct causes -- both are modeled as distinct FailureMode nodes with the underlying under-threading treated as the chain origin (CAUSED_BY cause). No explicit EIIS code given for the actuator, cover plate, bolt, or o-ring components; left eiis_code null per rule 2. Two previous similar LERs referenced as stubs with keys copied exactly as stated in narrative. No backup systems described as operable during this event (bypass valves inoperative due to low DEH pressure) so no BACKED_UP_BY edges emitted.
